title: Developer Kickoff: API Pricing & Quickstart Playbook (draft)
content:
Summary:
A compact playbook for the first 10 minutes and first 7 days of a developer's experience with Redwood's Hosted API. Focus: zero-friction quickstart flows, pricing language that reduces sticker shock, clear upgrade paths to Dedicated when teams need scale, and A/B test hypotheses for conversion optimization. This is a working draft — mix of copy, tactical experiments, and competitive notes.

Target audience and conversion goals:
- Audience: small engineering teams, indie makers, and platform / infra engineers evaluating an API-first LLM service.
- Short-term goals (activation): get a functional request within 10 minutes, surface token-cost estimate in the UI/CLI, and record first successful embed/generation event.
- Mid-term goal (7 days): reach 10–50k tokens usage, establish billing card on file, and present Dedicated/Demo options for predictable throughput.

Core developer-first value props (single-line hooks):
- "Start building in minutes — same API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- "Predictable latency, transparent token economics, and SDKs that just work."
- "Move from experiment to production with zero code changes for routing and scale."

Quickstart angles (UX flows to test):
1) 3-step CLI flow (fastest path): signup -> api-key copy -> run `rw api example` (includes a one-off sample with inline token-estimate).
   - Microcopy: "Your first response in < 10s — token cost shown before you hit send."
   - CTA: "Run sample" (no credit card)
2) In-browser interactive quickstart (visual sandbox): pre-populated prompt templates (chat, summarize, Q&A), live token meter, toggle: "lower-cost mode" (auto quantize/model fallback).
   - CTA: "Try sandbox" -> record email, option to save sample to project.
3) SDK snippet embed in README (for GitHub rows): single-file example in top-level repo README with badges that show free credits remaining.

Pricing-language draft (tone: engineer-trustworthy, avoid marketing fluff):
- Headline: "Pay for what you consume — transparent per-token pricing and predictable upgrade options."
- Short blurb: "Per-request token billing with explicit request previews and cost estimate. Switch to Reserved capacity for steady workloads and lower per-token economics."
- Pricing ladder language (UI presentation):
   - "Free tier: 100k tokens/month — great for prototypes and testing."
   - "Pay-as-you-go: billed monthly, no upfront commits."
   - "Reserved (Dedicated): discounted unit rates for committed throughput. Contact Sales for region/on-prem options."
- Microcopy to reduce sticker shock: always show a per-request estimate inline and a projected monthly cost if current usage continues.

Competitive positioning shorthand (notes for comms team):
- Versus Generic Cloud AI endpoints: emphasize consistent output latency and **routing fallback** (region/model variant) for availability — not just model access.
- Versus model marketplaces: emphasize unified runtime + telemetry (token-level cost, latency breakdowns, request traces) and a single API for export to Dedicated or Private.
- Versus API-first competitors focusing on simplicity only: emphasize developer experience + production controls (canary rollouts, autoscale policies, billing transparency).

Suggested microcopy snippets for product surfaces (short, A/B-able):
- Signup success modal: "Welcome! Your API key is ready — run your first request and see an estimated cost before you send it."
- In-console token estimate label: "Estimated cost: $0.0012 — full breakdown available in Usage tab."
- Billing CTA on small teams page: "Keep experimenting — upgrade to Reserved for predictable costs and priority capacity."

A/B test ideas (priority order):
- A1: Show per-request dollar estimate vs. only token counts at quickstart — measure signup -> card-on-file conversion.
- A2: Display free-tier timer/credits badge in README snippets vs. not — measure GitHub click-throughs.
- A3: Inline cheaper-mode toggle (auto-quantize model variant) vs. hidden in advanced settings — measure toggles used and retention.

Customer objection handling (quick lines):
- "How do I avoid surprise bills?" -> "We preview estimated cost before every request and send usage alerts at thresholds you control."
- "Can I maintain latency if I save money?" -> "Routing policies ensure low-latency variants first; cheaper fallbacks are used only when you opt in or capacity is constrained."

Launch checklist (minimum for initial rollout):
- [ ] CLI new-user flow implemented with token preview (engineering ticket: RED-UX-321).
- [ ] Sandbox page with templates + toggle implemented (design: Maya, eng: Jon).
- [ ] Billing microcopy deployed across modal and usage page.
- [ ] A/B test 1 instrumentation in analytics (KPI: card-on-file rate).
- [ ] Copy deck for support and documentation written (this doc -> support playbook).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Free tier size: 50k vs 100k tokens — tradeoffs: conversion vs. abuse surface. (Ops input: Riley)
- Default model for quickstart: full-quality model vs. cheaper small-LM. Which better demonstrates latency/quality?
- Recommended default for sandbox: enable cheaper-mode toggle by default? (privacy/regulatory concerns if fallback crosses regions)

Notes from competitive scan (quick bullets, informal):
- Competitor A: shows only token counts in quickstart; users confused about $ impact -> opportunity to lead with $ estimates.
- Competitor B: advertises free tier but has complex reserved contracts — call out simplicity of pay-as-you-go + optional reserve.
- Competitor C: strong SDKs but poor telemetry; our differentiator is granular tracing + per-request cost breakdown.

Next steps / ownership:
- Iterate microcopy with Design and Docs (Riley to lead reviews).
- Implement A/B test A1 in staging by next sprint (Jon).
- Run a 2-week pilot with 3 small accounts to validate token-preview clarity and cost alerts (Maya to coordinate).

Quick links and refs (working):
- Tech: infra-issue RED-OPS-778 (token-meter backend).
- Docs: /docs/api/quickstart (WIP).
- Slack threads: #g2m-onboarding, #dev-velocity

Raw brainstorming fragments (keep here for context):
- "badge: 100k free tokens" vs "badge: $10 free credit" — which converts?
- Consider an onboarding flow that runs a short eval and shows expected monthly cost if scaled to 100k reqs/day (scare/educate).
- Could we instrument a "cost-simulate" mode that replays a sample project and shows monthly projection?

END DRAFT

(Do not treat as final comms. This doc should inform the first rollout and the A/B tests; preserve versioning.)
